fixed: A card reading STEAL was tied to the ball Nick put his hand on, and it lay over his face. It is gone: he puts a hand on one ball, and the narrator and the gold word in the caption say which.
The two shopkeepers stood so close that their pointing hands met like a fist bump. They stand further apart, each by a stall.
Two students stood half on top of each other. They stand apart, close enough that the one on the right is whole inside the tall picture too.
You and the Stranger were set on the same spot for the last picture. You now stop a step from him, behind the desk.
notes: Nick and Ibrahim are plain white-headed figures in a dark blue jacket and a tan shirt, not likenesses, and neither is given a word. Ibrahim's thought is a note of his two options: STEAL: NOTHING, SPLIT: A CHANCE.
The host is a figure in a red jacket who stands behind the desk and shrugs toward Ibrahim for one shot.

The balls open in red light one after the other: Ibrahim's on SPLIT under The balls open, then Nick's on SPLIT under Nick split too. Then the light turns pale, the pile parts in two and both throw up their hands.

The list sentence is cut at its commas into four spoken lines, so price wars, group projects and a shared kitchen each have a picture of their own for about a second and a half: two shopkeepers pointing at each other over 50% OFF and 60% OFF, one student working while two watch, two flatmates and a pile of unwashed cups. The two golden balls are in each. No word of the sentence is changed; there is a short breath after each thing. No laptop and no sink are drawn.
I watched the three everyday pictures frame by frame from the preview, since no strip is cut where the people change.
The ending: you stand up, walk round behind the desk and stop beside the Stranger, who is surprised and then smiles. You do not push the balls aside; they are left untouched on the desk.
Short shots on purpose: Think about it (1.4 s), So he splits (1.5 s) and the three everyday pictures. Two shots run 4.4 s, each on one long clause.
For one frame after a cut a face is half way between two expressions, as on every cut that keeps someone on screen.

Sound: tense music through Nick's game, a click as each ball opens, applause under Nick split too, then the hopeful music to the end and one bell on the last word. Claude cannot hear; this is for Biku's ears.
This part is 46.8 s. With parts 1 and 2 the whole video comes to about 2 minutes 7.
